title: Citrus juice in place of a recipe's liquid
reason: The sources use lemon juice to sour or brighten a liquid at no more than 1 tablespoon per cup of it, never as the liquid itself.

evidence.basis: Knowledge packet 2026-10-13b item L1, PROPOSED (not approved). Found tracing the popovers card (7/8 cup lemon juice for 7/8 cup milk). Research lemon_juice_1to1_for_wine_at_deglaze (PARTIALLY_SOURCED): "No source endorses undiluted lemon juice at the wine's full volume. Sourced acid amounts are 1/48 to 1/16"; lemon juice pH 2.03-2.62 (SRC-AC-10, SRC-AC-11, SRC-AC-26). E2's sources: 1 tbsp acid per cup of milk (King Arthur SRC-CM-26#a; USU, NDSU/Purdue, OSU, Illinois, NC State, Land O'Lakes). The ceiling 1/16 (1 tbsp per cup) is the largest sourced amount. Lemon juice is the only citrus juice in the vocabulary; vinegar has no kind, so vinegar as a liquid is NOT limited (known gap).
